verses.text: A song of ascents. LORD, remember David and everything he went through.
Remember how he swore to the LORD and made a promise to the Mighty One of Jacob:
“I won’t step inside my house or climb into my bed.
I won’t close my eyes and sleep or even let myself doze
until I find a place for the LORD, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
We heard about it in Ephrathah and found it in the field of Jaar.
“Let’s go to his home. Let’s bow down and worship at his footstool.”
Rise up, LORD, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
Dress your priests in righteousness, and let your faithful people shout for joy!
For the sake of your servant David, don’t turn your anointed one away.
The LORD gave David his word, and he’ll keep it: “I’ll put one of your own descendants on your throne.
If your children keep my covenant and the teaching I give them, their children will sit on your throne forever.”
The LORD chose Zion. That’s where he wanted to make his home.
“This is my resting place forever. I’ll live here because this is where I want to be.
I’ll bless it with plenty of food. I’ll give its poor enough bread to eat their fill.
I’ll dress its priests in salvation, and its faithful people will shout for joy.
There I’ll make David’s horn sprout. I’ve set a lamp in place for my anointed one.
I’ll dress his enemies in shame, and his own crown will shine.”
